The test image shows a corn stalk node with dark black/brown discoloration concentrated at the node. The stalk itself looks otherwise green/healthy. This is a stem symptom.

Key features: black node discoloration, stalk appears intact otherwise.

Top candidate: **Physoderma_Stalk_Rot** — "Black nodes at first or second node, pith rot, nodes that snap easily when pushed."

The reference image for Physoderma_Stalk_Rot shows scattered dark spots on the internode surface. The test image shows a more solid/concentrated dark black band specifically at the node, with the stalk otherwise green. This node blackening is actually the defining feature of Physoderma_Stalk_Rot: "Black nodes at first or second node."

The match is strong: dark/black discoloration concentrated at the node, green stalk otherwise intact, leaf sheath being peeled back to reveal the black node.
